title: Representation Router
subtitle: Representation Router applied to itself
mission: Turn software-engineering semantics into task-, audience-, and context-appropriate visual, interactive, textual, or composite working representations while preserving identity, meaning, evidence, provenance, and authority boundaries.
productThesis: A person should be able to participate in end-to-end software engineering by starting from the job they are trying to do, while Representation Router chooses and coordinates the representations, working surfaces, implementation paths, and evidence needed underneath.
coreRule: Lead with the job. Teach the technical language in context. Preserve the exact truth underneath.

currentCheckpoint.label: Consolidation v0 / PR #23 landing review
currentCheckpoint.question: Is the consolidated Representation Router boundary now clear, falsifiable, and small enough to land without promoting unearned evidence, projection, provider, or workflow abstractions?

nextCheckpoint.label: External Product / Environment Connector
nextCheckpoint.why: Capability expansion remains deferred until a real product-owned deployment/observability target and explicit authority exist. Consolidation does not authorize another local proving sandbox.

phases.label: Representation foundation
phases.summary: Choose useful representations from semantic structure, human intent, interaction needs, scale, and constraints.

phases.label: Working surfaces
phases.summary: Coordinate several views, revisions, provenance, shared focus, and honest action boundaries.

phases.label: Human comprehension
phases.summary: Make architecture and review surfaces interactive and understandable without requiring RR vocabulary first.

phases.label: Author + implement
phases.summary: Turn human-authored feature intent into supported implementation candidates and executed evidence.

phases.label: Task-first end-to-end workflow
phases.summary: Start from Build, Fix, Understand, Review, or Release and route into the right working surface.

phases.label: Release + operate
phases.summary: Prove deployment, observation, rollback, and re-release inside an explicitly owned staging boundary.

phases.label: Understand RR itself
phases.summary: Use Representation Router to represent its own architecture, roadmap, capability, plans, and evidence.

phases.label: Consolidate the reusable boundary
phases.summary: Harden contracts, separate source semantics from representations/providers, measure core/reference coupling, and prefer no new abstraction when evidence does not earn one.

phases.label: Real product connection
phases.summary: Connect product-owned deployment and observability authority instead of extending the local proving sandbox.

milestones.label: Representation routing core
milestones.why: Choose the representation before choosing a rendering library.
milestones.proved: The repository can filter/rank representation patterns, produce ViewSpecs, infer interactions, and route implementation/playbook/quality guidance.
milestones.lesson: A data shape is not enough; concern, task, scale, interaction, availability, provenance, and learning goals affect representation choice.

milestones.label: SurfaceSpec working-surface layer
milestones.why: A useful engineering workspace often coordinates several representations and authoritative sources rather than showing one diagram.
milestones.proved: RR can describe a source/revision-bound working surface with shared semantic focus and explicit read-only/local/authoritative action boundaries.
milestones.lesson: A visible control does not gain authority merely because it exists.

milestones.label: Review Workbench + architecture lenses
milestones.why: Test whether RR can make a real repository change easier to understand than raw files and PR history.
milestones.proved: The same change can be reviewed through linked architecture, requirements, evidence, and provenance views.
milestones.lesson: Green automation and human usefulness are separate states.

milestones.label: Interactive + task-first comprehension
milestones.why: Static diagrams and internal RR terminology were still too hard to use.
milestones.proved: Graphs became draggable/inspectable and the primary UI moved to ordinary task language with technical depth disclosed later.
milestones.lesson: The interface should describe the human job, not the graph algorithm or RR implementation vocabulary.

milestones.label: First real vertical feature: Saved Graph Layouts
milestones.why: Move from explaining/reviewing software work to building a real feature end to end.
milestones.proved: Presentation layout can be persisted separately from semantic architecture truth and bound to an exact revision.
milestones.lesson: Remembering presentation state must not become semantic-model mutation.

milestones.label: Feature Studio guided authoring
milestones.why: Let a person author engineering intent before starting in the codebase.
milestones.proved: Outcome, behavior decisions, acceptance scenarios, impact, and a structured implementation brief can be authored in a task-first surface.
milestones.lesson: Engineering intent is real work, but it is not yet implementation or executed evidence.

milestones.label: Implementation Loop + Runner
milestones.why: Close the loop from authored intent to candidate code/artifact and executed checks.
milestones.proved: Supported briefs route through known adapters into deterministic candidate runtimes, CI evidence, and human review while unsupported work abstains.
milestones.lesson: Brief ≠ code; test definition ≠ executed test; green CI ≠ human acceptance.

milestones.label: Multi-feature adapter coverage
milestones.why: One saved-layout adapter did not prove the runner was feature-general.
milestones.proved: The same runner core handles Saved Graph Layouts and Evidence Gap Focus through different adapters/runtimes and abstains on unsupported work.
milestones.lesson: Feature-specific decision vocabularies belong in adapters, not the generic runner core.

milestones.label: Engineering Home
milestones.why: People should start from the engineering job, not from names of RR artifacts.
milestones.proved: Build, Fix, Understand, Review, and Release can be routed with explicit ready/partial/unavailable states.
milestones.lesson: A card existing is not evidence that a workflow is supported.

milestones.label: Generic Build + Fix authoring
milestones.why: Build authoring was feature-specific and Fix had no typed diagnostic-to-implementation path.
milestones.proved: Two feature families can be authored generically; one typed problem family can diagnose to a normal implementation brief and runner candidate.
milestones.lesson: Build and Fix should converge on shared implementation/evidence contracts rather than fork into unrelated engines.

milestones.label: Release + Operate Loop v0
milestones.why: The lifecycle still stopped before deployment, runtime observation, and rollback.
milestones.proved: Repository CI can deploy an exact Home bundle to its own staging sandbox, observe staged routes over HTTP, roll back to retained bytes, verify rollback, and re-apply the intended release.
milestones.lesson: Staging authority and staging evidence do not imply production authority or production reliability.

milestones.label: Representation Router Self Map v0
milestones.why: The project accumulated enough artifacts and checkpoints that the user lost the project-level mental model.
milestones.proved: A source-bound, single-file RR surface represents the project through linked roadmap, architecture, capability, evidence, and plans; the consolidation refresh keeps current project state in that model.
milestones.lesson: A project self-map must be refreshed when project authority/state changes; exact revision binding alone does not make stale semantics current.

milestones.label: Consolidation v0
milestones.why: The proving portfolio had grown faster than the reusable boundary could be explained, validated, and falsified.
milestones.proved: Runtime public-contract validation is executable; required-vs-observed evidence remains adapter-owned; architecture semantics cross a provider-neutral RR boundary and render through real Structurizr without source/provider authority drift; abstention/complement analysis found no justified confidence threshold or universal set-selection contract; measured coupling does not justify a mass directory move.
milestones.lesson: Promote only evidence-earned invariants and boundaries. A useful experiment can end with no new core abstraction.

milestones.label: External Product / Environment Connector
milestones.why: The next missing capability is real product-owned deployment and observability, not another local sandbox.
milestones.lesson: Requires a real target identity, permission boundary, approval/stale policy, deployment receipt, telemetry provenance, and rollback authority.

milestones.label: General incident / operate workflows
milestones.why: Fix/Operate still use narrow proving cases rather than real logs, traces, metrics, and incidents.
milestones.lesson: Operational diagnosis must preserve uncertainty and source-owned runtime truth.

nodes.label: Domain / workflow truth
nodes.plain: The software, planning, architecture, evidence, runtime, or product facts RR is trying to help someone work with.

nodes.label: Representation choice
nodes.plain: Figure out what kind of view makes the current question easiest to answer.
nodes.technical: router.mjs: hard constraints + explainable scoring + ViewSpec construction

nodes.label: Source-neutral architecture seam
nodes.plain: Receive source-owned architecture facts without teaching RR the source system's planning/review ontology or a renderer's vocabulary.
nodes.technical: architecture-candidate.mjs: experimental ArchitectureViewCandidate validation + concern availability

nodes.label: Architecture provider adapter
nodes.plain: Render only architecture concerns the source actually supports, and abstain when a provider cannot represent an available concern.

nodes.label: Representation plan
nodes.plain: Add interactions, implementation approach, interface patterns, construction guidance, and quality checks to the selected representation.

nodes.label: Working surface contract
nodes.plain: Coordinate several views, sources, revisions, shared focus, and safe actions into one human workspace.

nodes.label: Engineering intent authoring
nodes.plain: Turn supported human product decisions into a structured implementation brief without starting in code.

nodes.label: Problem diagnosis routing
nodes.plain: For supported problem families, turn observed-vs-expected behavior into a diagnosis and normal implementation brief; otherwise abstain.

nodes.label: Supported implementation routing
nodes.plain: Choose a registered implementation adapter/runtime for a brief, preview the plan, build a candidate, or say the work is unsupported.

nodes.label: Task-first engineering surfaces
nodes.plain: Let a person begin with Build, Fix, Understand, Review, or Release and enter the appropriate workspace.
nodes.technical: Engineering Home / Engineering Studio / Review Workbench proving surfaces

nodes.label: Execution evidence
nodes.plain: Actually run tests/builds and retain artifacts so the project can distinguish planned checks from checks that executed.

nodes.label: Release / runtime evidence
nodes.plain: Describe a release target and authority, record what bytes deployed, what was observed, and whether rollback really restored the previous bytes.

nodes.label: Human judgment
nodes.plain: Decide whether the representation, feature behavior, review result, or release is actually acceptable/useful.
nodes.technical: Human review remains separate from automated verification

edges.label: answers a concern about
edges.meaning: RR routes a concern over source-owned truth into candidate representations.
edges.nonclaim: RR does not become the semantic or workflow authority for the source domain.

edges.label: selected view feeds
edges.meaning: The chosen ViewSpec is enriched with interactions, implementation routing, interface patterns, playbook, and quality guidance.
edges.nonclaim: A library choice is not the representation decision itself.

edges.label: can compose into
edges.meaning: One or more concern-specific views can participate in a source-bound working surface.
edges.nonclaim: Not every representation requires SurfaceSpec; a simple view may stand alone.

edges.label: guides
edges.meaning: Working-surface contracts and task-first language inform product/proving interfaces.
edges.nonclaim: SurfaceSpec does not own product persistence, authorization, or effects.

edges.label: hands off brief to
edges.meaning: Supported authored intent becomes implementation-brief/v1 and enters the implementation router.
edges.nonclaim: An authored brief is not code and does not prove checks executed.

edges.label: converges on
edges.meaning: A supported diagnosis produces the same implementation-brief/v1 contract used by Build authoring.
edges.nonclaim: Unknown problem families are not guessed into a fix.

edges.label: Build enters
edges.meaning: Task-first Build routes into adapter-driven engineering intent authoring.
edges.nonclaim: Engineering Home navigation does not grant implementation authority.

edges.label: Fix enters
edges.meaning: Task-first Fix can enter a typed problem/diagnosis workflow for supported problem families.
edges.nonclaim: Current diagnostic coverage is narrow, not general debugging intelligence.

edges.label: verified by
edges.meaning: Generated candidates only become executed evidence when the repository CI path actually runs the named checks/builds.
edges.nonclaim: A test definition or planned check is not execution evidence.

edges.label: provides exact artifact to
edges.meaning: Release/Operate uses exact CI-built artifact bytes and a repository-owned staging authority in the proving loop.
edges.nonclaim: CI staging evidence does not imply production deployment authority.

edges.label: informs
edges.meaning: Executed automation provides evidence a human can review.
edges.nonclaim: Green CI does not decide product usefulness, review acceptance, or semantic correctness beyond the checks that ran.

edges.label: returns evidence to
edges.meaning: Deployment/observation/rollback evidence is presented for human interpretation and acceptance.
edges.nonclaim: A successful staging release is not a production approval.

edges.label: projects architecture semantics into
edges.meaning: A domain owner can expose an architecture-only candidate with stable identities, boundaries, contracts, relationships, behaviors, and exact provenance.
edges.nonclaim: RR does not parse planning/review presentation state to reconstruct architecture, and the candidate does not choose a renderer.

edges.label: routes available concerns to
edges.meaning: RR derives concern availability from source semantics, then an experimental provider adapter renders only concerns it supports.
edges.nonclaim: Provider failure does not imply semantic absence; deployment can be semantically available while Structurizr currently abstains.

capabilities.label: Understand software
capabilities.summary: Task-first architecture/comprehension surfaces with component, sequence, state, relationships, requirements, evidence, and provenance.
capabilities.limit: Proven strongly on current RR/review examples; not universal reverse engineering.

capabilities.label: Review a change
capabilities.summary: Evidence-focused review can separate implementation, test definitions, executed evidence, source provenance, and pending human judgment.

capabilities.label: Author a feature
capabilities.summary: Engineering Studio can author implementation-brief/v1 for two verified feature families.
capabilities.limit: Authoring/adapter coverage is still narrow relative to arbitrary product work.

capabilities.label: Diagnose and fix
capabilities.summary: One typed reset-safety problem can diagnose into the same implementation/evidence path used by Build.
capabilities.limit: No general logs/traces/metrics-driven debugging or broad diagnostic adapter coverage yet.

capabilities.label: Implement supported changes
capabilities.summary: Implementation Runner supports two feature adapters/runtimes, deterministic dry-run plans, candidates, and explicit abstention.
capabilities.limit: It is not arbitrary code synthesis for unknown features.

capabilities.label: Verify supported work
capabilities.summary: Exact CI checks and retained artifacts are linked to supported Build/Fix/release proving loops.
capabilities.limit: Evidence only covers checks that actually ran; it does not prove untested behavior or human acceptance.

capabilities.label: Release
capabilities.summary: CI staging deploy/observe/rollback/re-release is implemented with exact byte receipts.
capabilities.limit: Production/external environment authority is not connected.

capabilities.label: Observe runtime
capabilities.summary: The staging loop serves the deployed directory and records HTTP observations after deploy, rollback, and re-apply.
capabilities.limit: No external telemetry, logs, traces, metrics, or incident workflow is connected.

capabilities.label: Real product / production connection
capabilities.summary: No production deployment or external observability connector exists.
capabilities.limit: Requires a real product-owned target, permissions/credentials, approval and stale-revision policies, telemetry provenance, and rollback authority.

evidence.label: SurfaceSpec contract proved and merged
evidence.claim: RR can coordinate source-bound working surfaces without absorbing domain authority.
evidence.proof: PR #22 merged after exact CI execution; the repository retains schema/builder/proving cases.
evidence.doesNotProve: That every downstream working surface is understandable or useful.

evidence.label: Interactive review artifacts built in CI
evidence.claim: Architecture/review representations can be interactive, source-linked, and task-first.
evidence.proof: Review Workbench versions are built in repository CI and retained as artifacts.
evidence.doesNotProve: That the user accepts every interaction or wording choice.

evidence.label: Implementation Runner executed
evidence.claim: A supported implementation brief can route to a deterministic adapter/runtime candidate and execution receipt.
evidence.proof: Implementation Runner plans/builds/receipts are exercised by tests and GitHub Actions.
evidence.doesNotProve: That arbitrary unknown software changes can be implemented safely.

evidence.label: Two distinct feature families use the same runner core
evidence.claim: The runner is not only a Saved Graph Layouts shell.
evidence.proof: Saved Graph Layouts and Evidence Gap Focus use separate adapters/runtimes while generic brief normalization/routing is shared.

evidence.label: Build and Fix converge on one handoff
evidence.claim: Supported authored features and supported diagnosed problems can both produce implementation-brief/v1 and enter the same implementation/evidence path.
evidence.proof: Engineering Studio + Fix proving path are built and retained in CI.
evidence.doesNotProve: General debugging or arbitrary feature authoring.

evidence.label: CI staging deployment + observation + rollback executed
evidence.claim: RR can represent and prove a repository-owned staging release lifecycle with exact bytes, HTTP observations, rollback, and re-apply.
evidence.proof: Release + Operate Loop v0 and exact refreshed-Home staging proof pass in GitHub Actions.
evidence.doesNotProve: Production deployment authority, external telemetry, production reliability, or human acceptance.

evidence.label: Self Map source/model checks
evidence.claim: The Self Map model, references, interaction contract, and single-file build have executable checks.
evidence.proof: The Self Map model/reference/interaction/browser-review checks are configured in repository CI. Execution status belongs to the exact CI run shown in this artifact's build snapshot rather than to this static model.
evidence.doesNotProve: A configured check does not prove it executed successfully; inspect the exact build snapshot/run. Even a green run does not prove human comprehension or usefulness.

evidence.label: Consolidation v0 exact-head regression evidence
evidence.claim: The consolidation boundary, runtime contracts, T3B provider experiment, and abstention/complement regressions pass on the landed project branch.
evidence.proof: PR #24 exact-head CI passed before merge; after merge into PR #23, the parent branch CI rebuilt the complete proving portfolio successfully.
evidence.doesNotProve: Human usefulness of every surface, production/external capability, or that experimental ArchitectureViewCandidate/Structurizr policy should be promoted as a public default.

authorityBoundaries: RR does not own domain/workflow semantic truth merely because it renders or coordinates it.
RR browser surfaces do not gain Git, planning, review-approval, production deployment, or telemetry authority by exposing controls.
A test definition is not evidence the test executed.
Green CI is not human acceptance.
A staging deployment is not a production deployment.
Dragging or arranging a representation changes presentation state unless an explicit authoritative contract says otherwise.
